procedure: EA-NEGONT-02 v0.7 §3.4 D/R/O (working; not frozen). Admission by reading: D, a claim on what a literary heteronym is, how it differs from a pseudonym, what an orthonym is, who practised it (Pessoa, Kierkegaard, Yeats, Machado, antiquity) or how the concept can be tested; R, a relation between the concept and an archive object (the PKG, the corpus seats, the authorship investigation, the Crimson Hexagon); O, an archive category applied to it (meta-heteronym, cross-substrate heteronym, structure-function, the No-Floor Theorem, the firewall, the symbolon, the functional orthonym, heteronymy as ethical practice). The archive's own Dodecad practice is the separate entity heteronymy-dodecad; general claims about heteronymy made in Dodecad documents are admitted, rosters and protocols are not. Machine compositions recorded in deposits are reception evidence and are not admitted. Volume is never a ground of removal; instances of one work, and restatements of one claim, are grouped as a lineage and kept.
